documents.content: The student writes a condition that does not express when the loop should keep running. Typical form: describing when to stop (while x == target) rather than when to continue (while x != target), testing a variable the loop body never changes, or reversing the comparison direction. The difference from LOOP-01 is that the error is not off by one; the loop can run zero times, the wrong number of times by a large margin, or never. Difference from LOOP-05: here the faulty artifact is the condition itself.

diagnostic_signals: A recursive call appears as a statement with no return or combination expression.
The base case is reached but the top-level result is None or equals only the base value.
A trace shows a valid sub-result being computed then ignored by its caller.
counter_signals: The learner predicts pre/post-call execution order incorrectly, suggesting REC-24.
The non-recursive function prints instead of returning, suggesting FUNC-17.
A non-recursive return is absent on one path or placed too early, suggesting FUNC-18.
source_citations: Catalogs of C and Python Antipatterns by CS1 Students
An Inquisitive Code Editor for Addressing Novice Programmers' Misconceptions of Program Behavior
